answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a stake that grows with each new identity: every agent must lock 500 POA as a bond before its first task, refundable only after 30 days of honest work. Like a harbor that charges each ship a berthing fee, the cost compounds - spawning 1,000 fake agents would tie up 500,000 POA. An orchard grows one tree per seed, not a forest from one; likewise a karst landscape lets water through only narrow cracks, so cheap mass identities simply cannot flood the system.
